solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Trophy's displayed over Los Angeles Dome

parts.note: a trophy is a cup, the possessive 's adding no letter
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A trophy is put on show above the Los Angeles skyline's great dome.
explanation.definitionFit: A rounded roof or small domed tower on a building is called by this architectural term.

clue.text: Special troop with positive attitude collecting old Military Medal

indicators.note: collecting means the attitude word gathers the other letters within it

parts.note: a can-do attitude is a positive, willing one
MM is the abbreviation for the Military Medal, a British gallantry award

explanation.surface: A soldier with a confident approach picks up an old gallantry medal.
explanation.definitionFit: These are soldiers trained for raids, a special forces unit or member of one.

clue.text: Under tree, place monkey's swallowed fruit

indicators.note: in a down clue, under puts the rest beneath the tree word

parts.note: a pine is a coniferous tree

indicators.note: swallowed means the primate word takes the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: an ape is a monkey-like primate; the 's is the link has
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: Beneath a tree, a monkey has gulped down some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a tropical fruit with spiky skin and sweet yellow flesh.

clue.text: Religious martyr, rigged trial snared me

indicators.note: snared means the reshuffled letters trap the other piece inside
a rigged trial is fixed, so the letters of the word are fixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man of faith complains that a fixed trial caught him out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rigged' makes LATIR, which then holds the second piece; Latimer was one of the Oxford Martyrs of Mary I's reign.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugh Latimer was a Protestant bishop burned at the stake in Oxford in 1555.

clue.text: Appropriate type of modern art

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to take something for oneself, to make off with it
non-representational art of shapes and colours rather than real objects

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to remove or steal; the other is the art movement that avoids depicting real things.

clue.text: Hippy perhaps sporting a denim bathrobe

indicators.note: sporting means playing about, so the words are frolicked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A hippy is seen wearing a bathrobe made of denim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hippy' looks like a flower child, but means wide in the hips.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone wide around the hips, so a hippy person is an example.

clue.text: Bit of a blow — ten around for dessert

parts.note: a tap is a light blow, a small bit of one
10 written as the letters I and O
ca is short for circa, meaning around

explanation.surface: Ten people gather for a pudding after a slight knock.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a milky pudding made from starch grains of cassava root.

clue.text: Middle Eastern president like Saddam — not half

parts.note: as means like, in the same way as

indicators.note: not half keeps only the first half of the dictator's name

explanation.surface: A leader in the Middle East is compared to Saddam, but only half as bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Hafez and Bashar al-Assad were successive presidents of Syria.

clue.text: Spruces up items of clothing worn by princess, affectionately remembered

indicators.note: worn by means the clothing word wraps around the princess

parts.note: ties are neckwear, items of clothing
Di was the familiar name for Diana, Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: Neckties once worn by a fondly remembered princess are smartened up.
explanation.definitionFit: To tidy something up is to make it neat, which is what sprucing does.

clue.text: Holder of extreme views to provide money for disruption of animal test

parts.note: to fund is to finance, to provide money for

indicators.note: disruption means the letters of the words after it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An extremist finances an attempt to disrupt animal testing.
explanation.definitionFit: This is someone who holds rigidly to strict basic doctrines, often religious, and rejects compromise.

clue.text: French artist delivers shock before time

indicators.note: before puts the hair word ahead of the time letter

parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick mass of it, a mane

explanation.surface: A French painter gives viewers a jolt just ahead of the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Édouard Manet was a nineteenth-century French painter linked to Impressionism.

clue.text: Peacekeeping organisation p-put forward without resistance

parts.note: UNO is the United Nations Organisation, which sends peacekeepers
the stammered p- gives an extra P, and put forward means posed, as a question is posed

explanation.surface: A stammering speaker says the UN was proposed with nobody objecting.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'p-put' is a stutter: it supplies a spare P before POSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unopposed meets no rival or objection, so it goes ahead with no resistance.

clue.text: Shocked in the style of jolly editor

parts.note: à la is French borrowed into English for in the manner of
a jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked by an editor who behaves in a cheerful way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' reads as cheerful, but in crosswords it is a Royal Marine (RM).
explanation.definitionFit: Being alarmed is being frightened or disturbed, much as a shock leaves someone.

clue.text: Exit stamp describing desperate effort

parts.note: an exit is a way out, a door
a die is a tool that stamps a design onto metal, as for coins

explanation.surface: A rubber stamp marked on the exit door shows how hard someone tried.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a last all-out attempt where failure is not an option.

clue.text: Go off with intellectual faculty, organised in groups

parts.note: to go off is to leave, to depart
using the powers of the mind, done in the mind

explanation.surface: An academic leaves a university faculty that is sorted into sections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faculty' suggests a university department, but here it is the mind's power.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranged by departments means divided into separate sections or groups.

clue.text: Detective officer initially entering the sea at Nice is poor timekeeper

indicators.note: entering means the detective and officer pieces go into the French sea

parts.note: la mer is French for the sea, Nice being in France
tec is short for detective

indicators.note: initially takes just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A detective arrives at the seafront in Nice, late as usual.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who habitually arrives after the agreed time keeps time poorly.

clue.text: Part of goal is to thwart lawyers

parts.note: to cross someone is to oppose or thwart them
the Bar is the collective name for barristers

explanation.surface: Lawyers block the move, as a goal frame stops a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The horizontal bar joining the two posts forms the top of a football goal.

clue.text: Dan waited there pathetically doomed not to make progress

indicators.note: pathetically suggests the letters of these three words are wretchedly jumbled

explanation.surface: Dan lingered sadly in a place where he was never going to get anywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship stalled and drifting cannot move forward, an idiom for a failed project.

clue.text: Dropping long stretch of time in underground cell

parts.note: dung is animal droppings
an eon is an immensely long period

explanation.surface: A prisoner spends ages in a cell, littering it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping' looks like a deletion signal, but it is a noun meaning excrement.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is a dark prison chamber below a castle.

clue.text: Rolled up with Miliband, damaged

parts.note: wound, as yarn or a spring is wound, means coiled or rolled up
Ed Miliband is a British Labour politician, former party leader

explanation.surface: A politician is beaten and rolled up, hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Injured or hurt, as by a blow or weapon.

clue.text: Like poor actor in court study

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them
a den is a private room for working, a study

explanation.surface: A bad actor is in court, rehearsing in a study.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff, expressionless performer is said to act in a wooden way.

clue.text: Thin material in newspaper article is unknown

parts.note: an organ is a publication speaking for a party or group
Z is one of the algebraic unknowns x, y, z
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper story that leaves something unexplained is flimsy stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces sit in the clue as newspaper, article, unknown, but the article letter comes last in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a sheer, stiff silk or synthetic fabric used for dresses and veils.

clue.text: Supernatural being — endless precious metal produced by 'em

indicators.note: endless means the metal word loses its final letter

parts.note: gold is a precious metal
taken as written, the apostrophe merely marking 'them'

explanation.surface: Endless gold made by them conjures a mysterious creature.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jewish folklore it is a clay figure brought to life by magic.

clue.text: Moves like a kangaroo born on Oz

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for born in biographies
oz is the abbreviation for ounces

explanation.surface: A creature born in Australia hops about as kangaroos do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oz' looks like Australia, which suits the kangaroo, but it is the weight abbreviation for ounces.
explanation.definitionFit: A kangaroo travels by springing up and down, which is what hopping repeatedly is.

clue.text: Active old reprobate's indulgent lifestyle on the continent

indicators.note: a reprobate is depraved, so the two words beside it are corrupted into a new order

explanation.surface: A lively elderly rogue lives a life of European pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian phrase means the sweet life of luxury and self-indulgence.

clue.text: Bishop after protest to get out of army

indicators.note: after places the bishop letter following the protest word

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop joins a march to protest and to be released from military service.
explanation.definitionFit: To be discharged from the forces is the military short form of demobilise.

clue.text: Put forward, could make a mention

indicators.note: could make says the letters of the following words can be rebuilt as something else

explanation.surface: A suggestion is offered, which might be called a mention.
explanation.definitionFit: To propose someone as a candidate is to formally submit their name.

clue.text: One who loves making fuss about king

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother, as in much ado
re means concerning, about
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A lover makes a great to-do over a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who worships or is devoted to another person is their fervent admirer.
